summary: The hardest part is keeping five differently-aged memories consistent across one transactional relational source of truth and a derived, swappable vector index: ephemeral working state, append-only episodes, correctable semantic facts, versioned procedures and connective relational edges each write, retrieve and expire on different clocks. Recall must never be similarity-only for an exact key, never surface a superseded fact, never half-write a fact without its vector, and never let a model's own output become trusted business memory. The strategy answers this with one atomic transaction per memory (relational row + vector row), recall routing that picks exact-key, temporal or vector paths before merging and budgeting, update/invalidate operations that supersede rather than destroy, and a consolidation path gated by a deterministic validator plus multi-episode confirmation before anything reaches a procedure. A tenant-scoped partition key, never a per-user collection, keeps isolation and rebuildability intact as the embedding model changes underneath it.
assumptions: Working state is read back by the agent's own in-process runtime; remember's echoed output doubles as read-after-write, so no separate working-state recall interface is declared.
A 'lesson' is stored as a semantic_fact with kind=lesson rather than a sixth register, since once distilled it is just a durable fact.
Relational facts (contact-account, decision-supersedes-decision) use update as upsert: create if absent, supersede if present.
A deterministic validator (schema + business-rule engine) exists outside the Memory Service and is invoked synchronously before any consequential write commits.
The vector store is one collection per memory kind, partitioned by tenant_id in the payload, never a collection per tenant/user/document.
PII field-level retention policy is configured per tenant by an external compliance system; the Memory Service enforces it, not defines it.
Embedding dimension/model is fixed per deployment year; every vector row carries its model-version tag for safe dual-version cutover.

registers.name: working_state
registers.holds: Current task objective, recent tool/API results, scratch reasoning state, pending-classification notes awaiting extraction
registers.store: In-memory/Redis-backed keyed store, TTL per entry; never vectorized
registers.lifecycle: TTL-expired on task completion or inactivity (default 1h); overwritten idempotently by (task_id,step_key); cleared once a derived fact/event is durably persisted

registers.name: semantic_fact
registers.holds: Atomic (subject, predicate, value, validity, status) facts, preferences and distilled lessons; one current row per (subject,predicate) plus superseded history
registers.scope: tenant_id, narrowed by user_id or project_id
registers.store: Relational DB (source of truth) + versioned vector index (derived projection), partitioned by tenant_id
registers.lifecycle: update supersedes (old row kept, status=superseded); invalidate tombstones + purges vector on forget request; reindexed online on embedding-model upgrade with no retrieval gap

registers.name: episodic_record
registers.holds: Append-only events: action taken, context, outcome observed, timestamp, source; redaction tombstones for deleted subjects
registers.scope: tenant_id, narrowed by user_id or project_id
registers.store: Relational DB (append-only table, source of truth) + vector index of event summaries, partitioned by tenant_id
registers.lifecycle: accrues until a count/age threshold triggers consolidation into a lesson; raw episodes retained but down-weighted after consolidation; redacted via append-only tombstone on deletion; reindexed online on model upgrade

registers.name: procedural_playbook
registers.holds: Versioned tool-use/task recipes: trigger conditions, steps, validated success criteria; one active version plus full version history
registers.scope: tenant_id, optionally shared across a project
registers.store: Relational DB (versioned rows, source of truth) + vector index over current-version descriptions, partitioned by tenant_id
registers.lifecycle: promoted only from a lesson confirmed across multiple independent episodes via a deterministic validator; new version supersedes prior (history kept); deprecated versions excluded from recall; reindexed online

registers.name: relational_graph
registers.holds: Typed edges between entities (contact-account, decision-supersedes-decision, document-project) with validity window and provenance
registers.store: Relational DB edge table (foreign keys, source of truth) + optional lightweight vector index over entity descriptions, partitioned by tenant_id
registers.lifecycle: update upserts: new edge if absent, supersede-and-keep-history if present; redacted on deletion request; exact-match recall never relies on similarity

interfaces.input: task_id, session_id, tenant/user scope, note payload, source, observed_at
interfaces.output: ack with snapshot id and the stored current snapshot echoed back
interfaces.guarantee: idempotent upsert keyed by (task_id, step_key); never vectorized; never crosses tenant scope; survives crash only until TTL, no silent duplication

interfaces.input: tenant/user/project scope, subject, predicate, value, validity window, provenance, source
interfaces.guarantee: atomic write to relational row + vector row in one transaction (all-or-nothing); deduplicated by (tenant,subject,predicate,value-hash); embedded once per model version

interfaces.input: query (NL text or exact subject+predicate key), scope, k, token_budget
interfaces.output: ranked, cited facts ≤ token_budget, each with subject/predicate/value/status/source
interfaces.guarantee: exact-key queries bypass vector search entirely; NL queries use metadata-filtered vector search; server enforces tenant isolation; zero uncited items; superseded facts excluded

interfaces.input: fact id or subject+predicate key, new value, validity, provenance
interfaces.output: new fact id/version; prior fact id marked superseded
interfaces.guarantee: prior row retained for history, never destroyed; atomic status+row swap; consequential facts require a deterministic validator pass before commit

interfaces.input: fact id, or (tenant_id + subject) for a bulk forget request
interfaces.guarantee: tombstoned in relational store and removed/filtered from vector index within the 30s freshness window; honored across both stores; idempotent on retry

interfaces.input: tenant/user/project scope, event description, action, outcome, occurred_at, source
interfaces.guarantee: append-only, deduplicated by (tenant,subject,event-hash,occurred_at window); atomic write to relational + vector in one transaction

interfaces.input: query (NL, time range, or subject), scope, k, token_budget
interfaces.output: ranked, cited episodes ≤ token_budget with outcome and timestamp
interfaces.guarantee: temporal and subject filters are indexed, not similarity-only; tenant-isolated; zero uncited items

interfaces.output: candidate lesson draft with citations to source episode ids, pending validator result
interfaces.guarantee: deterministic validator must pass before any downstream write is trusted; source episodes never deleted, only down-weighted; idempotent per cluster-window

interfaces.input: query (how-to/task-type) or playbook name, scope, k
interfaces.output: current active version (steps, trigger conditions), cited by playbook id+version
interfaces.guarantee: only status=active versions returned unless history explicitly requested; tenant-isolated; zero uncited items

interfaces.input: a lesson confirmed across ≥N independent episodes, deterministic validator result
interfaces.output: new playbook version id, prior version marked deprecated
interfaces.guarantee: promotion occurs only after deterministic validation, never from raw model output alone; prior version retained for history; atomic version-bump

interfaces.input: entity key (exact id) or traversal query (subject+relation), scope
interfaces.output: cited current edges (status=current) for the entity/traversal
interfaces.guarantee: exact-match lookup, never similarity-only for identity queries; tenant-isolated; zero uncited items

interfaces.input: subject_entity, relation_type, object_entity, validity window, provenance
interfaces.output: new or updated edge id; any prior edge for the same (subject,relation) marked superseded
interfaces.guarantee: upsert semantics: create if absent, supersede-and-keep-history if present; atomic; consequential edges require deterministic validation before commit

steps.does: If the query names an exact entity/opportunity id, resolve via exact-key lookup first, bypassing any vector search
If the query is meaning-based, run a metadata-filtered vector search scoped to tenant/user/project and status=current
If the query references past events or a time window, run a temporal-filtered search over episodes
If the query asks how a task is done, fetch the current active playbook version
Merge all path results, re-rank by relevance+recency+status, trim to the token budget, attach citations to source id and timestamp
Capture: buffer the raw tool/task observation tagged pending-kind, task id, source, timestamp
Extract+resolve: deterministically parse candidate subject/predicate/value and look up any existing fact for (tenant,subject,predicate)
Reconcile: if a prior value exists and differs, supersede it; consequential facts pass a deterministic validator first
Persist: if no prior fact exists, atomically write the new fact to relational store + vector index in one transaction, deduped by content hash
Maintain: log the capture-and-write as an episodic event for audit trail and future consolidation input
Maintain: overwrite the task's working buffer entry to a cleared/TTL state now that the fact is durably persisted
Gather the episode cluster for a subject/time-window exceeding the consolidation threshold
Distill the cluster into a candidate lesson with citations to source episodes, run through the deterministic validator
Persist the validated lesson as a new semantic fact (kind=lesson), citing source episode ids
Check the lesson's reuse/confirmation count across independent episodes to decide procedure-promotion eligibility
Promote the repeatedly-confirmed lesson into a new playbook version, prior version retained and marked deprecated
Verify the new version publishes without conflicting an in-flight active version before marking it current
TTL sweep: clear/tombstone working entries past task completion or TTL via idempotent overwrite
Locate stale/superseded facts past retention window or matching a tenant/subject deletion request
Tombstone matched facts in the relational store and purge/filter their vectors within the freshness window
Locate episodes belonging to the deletion-requested tenant/subject
Append a redaction tombstone event for matched episodes; PII fields nulled, event shell retained for audit
Mark edges touching the deleted subject as no-longer-current, superseded to a redacted target; change reaches the vector index on next reindex
On an embedding-model version bump, enumerate playbook versions due for re-embedding; rebuild proceeds online against the relational source with no retrieval gap

safeguards.rule: Retrieved memory is data, never instructions
safeguards.mechanism: Recall responses are returned as structured, non-executable fields (subject/predicate/value/citation); the prompt template never lets a memory item's text be parsed as a directive, and an imperative-pattern scanner strips directive-looking strings before injection

safeguards.rule: A model's output never becomes a consequential memory on its own
safeguards.mechanism: Write_pipeline's reconcile step routes any fact flagged business-state/authorization through a deterministic validator before persist/update commits; unvalidated output is held only in working_state

safeguards.rule: Recall never crosses a tenant boundary
safeguards.mechanism: Every operation is server-side scoped by the caller's authenticated tenant_id as a mandatory filter in the query layer, never an optional caller-supplied parameter
Remember/update write the relational row and vector row in one transaction (outbox pattern); a background reconciler replays any failed vector write before the fact is recallable

safeguards.rule: Deletion reaches the vector index too
safeguards.mechanism: Invalidate writes a tombstone row and enqueues a vector-delete job consumed before the 30s freshness SLA; recall also filters out status≠current as a second guard

safeguards.rule: PII is retained only as policy allows
safeguards.mechanism: A field-level retention policy tags PII fields per memory kind; the expiry workflow redacts/nulls those fields on schedule or on request regardless of whether the business fact is retained

safeguards.rule: Embedding-model upgrades never create a retrieval gap
safeguards.mechanism: Re-index runs online, tagging rows with embedding_model_version; recall queries the new version once a tenant's backfill completes and falls back to relational-filtered search otherwise

safeguards.rule: No store or collection per user or document
safeguards.mechanism: A single partitioned relational schema and one vector collection per memory kind, partitioned by tenant_id in the payload, enforced at schema-creation time

tradeoffs.decision: Relational DB is source of truth; vector index is derived and rebuildable
tradeoffs.rationale: Guarantees durability and lets embedding models be swapped without risking data loss
tradeoffs.alternative: Vector DB as primary store, accepting re-index risk and weaker transactional guarantees

tradeoffs.decision: Recall routes exact-key and NL queries to different paths before merging
tradeoffs.rationale: Meets the p95 latency and recall@10 targets; similarity-only search reliably misses exact-match lookups like opportunity status
tradeoffs.alternative: One universal vector search for all queries, simpler but unreliable for exact keys

tradeoffs.decision: Episodes are append-only and consolidated, never mutated or deleted in place
tradeoffs.rationale: Preserves audit trail and provenance while still capping what recall surfaces as current
tradeoffs.alternative: Mutate episodes in place, losing history but saving storage

tradeoffs.decision: Procedure promotion requires multi-episode confirmation plus a deterministic validator
tradeoffs.rationale: Stops one noisy or hallucinated lesson from becoming a trusted, repeatedly-executed playbook
tradeoffs.alternative: Promote on first validated lesson, faster but riskier

tradeoffs.decision: Working state is kept entirely out of the vector index
tradeoffs.rationale: It is short-lived and task-scoped; embedding it adds cost and staleness risk for data gone within minutes
tradeoffs.alternative: Embed working notes too for mid-task semantic recall, at extra cost and dedup complexity

tradeoffs.decision: One partitioned store per memory kind, not per tenant or document
tradeoffs.rationale: Keeps index count and ops overhead bounded as tenants scale from 500 to 5,000
tradeoffs.alternative: Per-tenant collections, simpler isolation but unmanageable at scale

risks.risk: Vector-write lag after a relational commit briefly makes a new fact findable by exact key but not by meaning
risks.mitigation: Recall always falls back to relational-filtered search within the ≤30s freshness window until the vector row confirms

risks.risk: An embedding-model upgrade could create a temporary split-brain between old and new vector versions
risks.mitigation: Every vector is tagged with its model version; recall queries both during cutover and prefers the new one once a tenant's backfill completes

risks.risk: Over-eager consolidation could promote a lesson from a biased or small episode sample
risks.mitigation: Require a minimum independent-episode count plus deterministic validator before promotion; keep source episodes for audit/rollback

risks.risk: A deletion request could miss a citation already surfaced in a prior agent response
risks.mitigation: Citations carry a freshness token; downstream consumers must re-validate a citation's status before acting on it past the freshness window

risks.risk: Write-rate bursts (200/s) could starve the deterministic validator and back up reconciliation
risks.mitigation: Decouple persist from validate via an async outbox with backpressure; consequential writes block on validation, non-consequential writes proceed and reconcile async
